hints: Look at the force / N against extension / m shape: a steep near-straight start followed by a long curved flatter part ending at breaking.
Remember the elastic region is the first part up to the elastic limit where the wire would return to zero extension, and the plastic region is the permanent deformation after that point.
Remember work done to break the wire is $W = \text{area under } F \text{ against } x$ from $0$ to the breaking extension, so check which shading covers the whole curve.
walkthrough: Identify the curve: force / N on the vertical axis against extension / m on the horizontal axis, starting steep and linear then bending to a flatter plastic flow before fracture.
State the rule for regions: the initial linear part obeys Hooke's law and is reversible, so it is the elastic region up to the elastic limit.
State the next part: beyond the elastic limit the extension is permanent, so the long flatter part to breaking is the plastic region.
State the rule for energy: for a variable force, work done is $W = \int F dx$, which is the total area between the curve and the extension axis from $0$ to breaking.
Compare the options: reject shading of only the first part or only the second part, and reject any graph with the two region labels swapped.
Only the graph with elastic first, plastic second, and all the area under the curve to breaking shaded satisfies all three conditions. This is option D

options.A: Labels for elastic and plastic regions are in the right order, but the shaded work done is only the small area under the elastic part, not to breaking.
options.B: The shaded area is the total area to breaking, but the elastic and plastic region labels are swapped.
options.C: Labels are in the right order, but the shaded work done excludes the elastic part and covers only the plastic part.
options.D: Elastic region is the initial steep part, plastic region is the later flatter part, and the shading is the total area under the force-extension curve to breaking.
